content: Flatulence can be alleviated by using an antifoaming agent such as simethicone, which is taken orally. Simethicone works by causing smaller gas bubbles in the gastrointestinal tract to coalesce into larger bubbles, making it easier for the gas to be expelled through burping or flatulence. To prevent flatulence, enzyme-based dietary supplements may be beneficial. Foods associated with flatulence often contain substances that are indigestible by humans. When these substances reach the large intestine intact, they can be fermented by intestinal bacteria, leading to gas production. Enzyme-based supplements function by breaking down these indigestible substances before they reach the large intestine, thereby preventing gas formation. These supplements are typically consumed alongside foods known to cause flatulence. It is crucial to pair the appropriate enzyme with the corresponding food. For example, when consuming beans or other vegetables high in complex carbohydrates, taking a product containing alpha-galactosidase, such as Beano, may be helpful. Similarly, individuals with lactose intolerance may benefit from taking a lactase-containing product, such as Lactaid, when consuming lactose-containing foods, as this can reduce flatulence. Simethicone is classified as an antifoaming agent. Enzyme-based dietary supplements include products like Beano (containing alpha-galactosidase) and lactase (found in products like Lactaid). Additionally, certain herbal remedies, such as epazote, are claimed to have antiflatulent properties and are traditionally used in Mexican cuisine for this purpose.
